title: BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT relative to a proposed Amendment to Contract No. C-140018 with Beveridge & Diamond PC for legal services pertaining to…
text:
[Council File 21-1188-S16]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT relative to a proposed Amendment to Contract No. C-140018 with Beveridge & Diamond PC for legal services pertaining to the July 11, 2021 flooding incident at the Hyperion Water Reclamation Plant.
Recommendation(s) for Council action, SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR:
1. APPROVE an amendment to Contract No. C-140018 with Beveridge & Diamond that increases the contract ceiling by $1.5 million, for a total contract amount of $7.45 million.
2. AUTHORIZE the City Attorney, or designee, to prepare Controller instructions for any necessary technical adjustments, subject to the approval of the City Administrative Officer (CAO); and, AUTHORIZE the Controller to implement the instructions.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
None submitted by the City Attorney. Neither the CAO nor the Chief Legislative Analyst has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
[The City Council may recess to Closed Session, pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1), (d) (2), and (e)(1), to confer with its legal counsel regarding exposure to litigation and to discuss the need for term extensions and additional funding for outside counsel contracts relative to the cases entitled Mecklenburg v. Hyperion Water Reclamation Plant, Los Angeles Superior Court (LASC) Case No. 21STCV28114 (pending personal injury litigation); Abdelnur v. City of Los Angeles, LASC Case No. 22STCV00153, and Konig v. City of Los Angeles, LASC Case No. 22STCV00970 (mass tort litigation); and, West Basin Municipal Water District v. City of Los Angeles, LASC Case No. 26STCV25456 (contractual and tort litigation). ]
summary: Raises the legal services contract with Beveridge & Diamond over the 2021 Hyperion flooding incident by $1.5 million, bringing the total to $7.45 million.
